description:
Welcome to the green lung of the Earth, where the air is thick with mist, humidity, and the layered chorus of a thousand hidden lives.Hosted by field researcher Beatriz Yara Sinclair, Feather & Frond is an immersive, slow-listening expedition deep into the canopy, understory, and waterways of the Amazon rainforest. We explore the extraordinary, intimate partnerships between tropical botany and avian life—unraveling how birds and plants shape each other’s survival in the most biodiverse habitat on the planet.Each episode brings you into the field to decode the biological marvels, acoustic landscapes, and intricate ecological networks of the jungle:• The Bucket Orchid & The Hummingbird — Epiphytic traps, perfume-collecting bees, and the hyper-precise geometry of the violet-fronted brilliant.
• The Royal Flycatcher — Masterpieces of riverside camouflage and the dazzling crimson crests hidden in the flooded forest gloom.
• The Screaming Piha — The loudest acoustic engine in the subcanopy and its silent role in planting ancient hardwood giants.
• The Hoatzin & Toxic Arums — A prehistoric leaf-fermenting marvel that traded flight for the superpower to digest poisonous marsh plants.
• The Potoo & Night-Blooming Forests — Eyelid optics, dead wood mimicry, and the moonlit pollination of giant canopy flowers.
• Army Ant Raids & Antbirds — Dancing on the edge of chaos to uncover how predatory swarms fuel forest floor regeneration.
• The Strangler Fig & Spangled Cotinga — A 200-year botanical siege that transforms a fallen giant into a living wooden cathedral.
• The Guianan Cock-of-the-Rock — Blazing orange leks in ancient sandstone caves, planting forests across bare granite slopes.
• The Amazonian Umbrellabird — Infrasonic sub-bass calls and the engineering of flooded river island palm groves.Step away from the rush of the modern world. Pull up a camp stool, let the rain fall against the broad leaves, and listen to the green world breathe.

title: What No One Tells You About Enterprise Resource Planning Software
author: Growth Lane
description:
Have you ever wondered why companies spend months choosing an ERP system, only to discover later that the difficult part wasn't buying the software at all?

It's everything that comes after.

People usually talk about the obvious things: finance, inventory, purchasing, reporting, automation.

But here's what often gets left out.

An ERP doesn't magically make a business organized.

It exposes how organized or disorganized—the business already is.

Imagine a company where sales has one way of handling orders, finance has another, and the warehouse has developed its own process over the years.

Now bring in a new ERP.

The software is perfectly capable of handling the work.

But the company still has to decide which process is actually the right one.

And that's where the real work begins.

Another thing nobody tells you is that not every business needs to customize everything.

In fact, too much customization can become a headache of its own.

The smarter approach is usually to keep standard functionality where it makes sense and only adapt the system when the business has a genuine reason to work differently.

Then there's the data.

An ERP can give you one platform, but that doesn't automatically mean you have one version of the truth.

If customer records, inventory figures, supplier information, and financial data aren't managed consistently, the ERP simply gives you a more sophisticated place to see the same confusion.

And here's another one.

Your ERP doesn't operate in isolation.

There may be CRM tools, warehouse systems, HR software, customer portals, analytics platforms, and custom applications around it.

The quality of those connections can matter just as much as the ERP itself.

This is one reason I find companies like Deister interesting.

Rather than treating ERP as a completely isolated product, Deister takes a broader enterprise application approach across areas such as ERP, WMS, CRM, analytics, and other business functions.

And that leads to perhaps the biggest thing people don't tell you about ERP.

You aren't really buying software.

You're choosing how your business will work with its information, its processes, and its people for years to come.

So before comparing feature lists, ask a much simpler question:

What do we actually want our business to be able to do better?

That answer should come before the software.

And it might completely change the way you evaluate your options.

title: Is Your Warehouse Ready for the Next Challenge?
author: Growth
description:
Let’s be honest. A warehouse can look completely under control from the outside—and still have problems hiding in the details.

You might have plenty of stock, a busy team, and trucks moving in and out all day. But then someone asks a simple question:

“Can we trace this batch?”

Or, “Do we actually have this item available?”

Or even, “Why does the system say we have 500 units when the warehouse team is finding something different?”

And suddenly, finding the answer takes more time than it should.

That’s often where warehouse software management makes a real difference.

The goal isn’t simply to put warehouse activities on a screen. It’s to make the movement of goods easier to understand and easier to control.

Think about what happens when stock arrives.

It needs to be received, identified, assigned to a location, and made available for the next step. Then comes picking, packing, shipping, returns, and all the updates happening in between.

A good warehouse management system keeps those movements connected.

And when your operation deals with batches or expiry dates, that visibility becomes even more important. You need to know not just how much stock you have, but which stock you have and where it has moved.

That’s where WMS software can take some of the pressure off the team.

Axional WMS, for example, supports stock management, warehouse locations, picking, traceability, logistics, batch and expiry-date management, and RF-based warehouse operations.

But here’s something many companies overlook.

Your warehouse is not an island.

What happens in the warehouse can affect purchasing, sales, customer commitments, and the rest of the supply chain. When warehouse information stays connected with the wider business, decisions become much easier to make.

That’s also why inventory management software should give you more than a stock number.

You want to understand what is available, where it is, how it is moving, and what needs attention.

Because the next challenge might not be a bigger warehouse.

It might be more orders.

More products.

Another location.

More demanding customers.

And your warehouse technology should be ready for that change.

So ask yourself one question:

Is your warehouse software helping your team keep up—or making them work around the system?

The answer might tell you more than any feature list ever could.

Learn more about Axional WMS and Deister Software at deister.io.

title: Grace in the Chaos
author: RayAnn
description: Life is beautiful, messy, funny, heartbreaking—and rarely goes according to plan. Grace in the Chaos is a real-life podcast about motherhood, nursing, raising kids, navigating special needs, small-town life, and finding humor in the middle of it all. Through honest stories, practical education, and conversations about the things we don’t always say out loud, RayAnn creates a place to laugh, learn, feel understood, and find a little grace in the chaos.

title: A Parents' Guide to Education
author: Alice and Luke
description: A Parents’ Guide to Education helps parents understand the key ideas behind how students learn. Hosted by experienced teachers, Alice and Luke, we break down complex educational concepts into simple, practical insights you can use to support your child in their learning and revision, especially through their GCSE years.

description: Gay, 50+, and Fabulous celebrates the wisdom, strength, and joy of being gay and over 50. If you’re tired of feeling invisible or overlooked, if you’re ready to step into your full power, authenticity, and vibrancy, you’re in the right place.

title: Little Known
author: Simon Kevin
description: Little Known is a fascinating facts podcast hosted by Simon Keven, where every episode explores 10 amazing facts about one incredible topic.From the Internet, the Pyramids of Egypt, the Eiffel Tower, and the Amazon Rainforest to space, animals, famous landmarks, inventions, ancient civilizations, oceans, and unexplained mysteries, each episode reveals surprising facts you may have never heard before.Simple, interesting, and easy to enjoy, Little Known is made for curious listeners who love discovering something new in every episode.Ten facts. One topic. Something new to learn every time.

title: The Staton Report
author: Tim Stating the Obvious LLC
description:
The Staton Report is a weekly conversation about the news, politics, policy, and leadership shaping America and the world.

I’m Tim Staton. After decades of military service and a career working with leaders, organizations, investigations, inspections, and accountability, I’ve learned that leadership isn’t just about what people say. It’s about the decisions they make, the consequences that follow, and how those decisions affect the people they lead.

That’s the perspective I bring to The Staton Report.

Each week, we’ll look beyond the headlines and ask the questions that matter: What actually happened? Why does it matter? Who is making the decisions? What are the consequences? And where do we go from here?

We’ll talk about Washington, national security, the economy, culture, leadership, policy, and the issues affecting everyday Americans. I’ll give you my perspective, but I’ll also challenge my own assumptions, ask difficult questions, and try to separate the facts from the noise.

This isn’t about pretending every issue is simple. And it isn’t about telling you what to think.

It’s about taking a step back, looking at the bigger picture, and having an honest conversation about what’s happening in our country and why it matters.

News. Politics. Analysis. Leadership.

The Staton Report.
Leadership. Policy. Perspective.

title: Drop the Good Christian Act
author: Evie Long
description:
Drop the Good Christian Act with Evie Long is a raw, filter-free Christian podcast for anyone who is exhausted from pretending.
I’ve been a Christian for years, but some days I still feel like a baby in Christ. I open the Bible and wonder if I even know what I’m doing. I wrestle with a prayer life that doesn't look like what I think it should, and I'm tired of performing spiritual maturity I don't actually have.
This isn't a teaching show for people who have it figured out. I'm not here with answers, and half the time I'm still working through my own questions. This is me pulling back the curtain on the real mess of trying to actually know Jesus. We are talking about the quiet doubt, the constant distractions, and the heavy pressure to look spiritually put-together for everyone watching.
If you are a Christian who is ready to stop playing a character and finally drop the performance, pull up a chair. We're figuring out our faith walk together from scratch. Hit follow so you don't miss an episode, and let's start pursuing Jesus for real.

title: History Was Stranger
author: Joe Holt
description:
History Was Stranger is a documentary history podcast about the people, scandals, rivalries, disasters, obsessions, and extraordinary decisions that made the past far stranger than the version we usually learn in school.
Each episode takes one remarkable true story from history and looks beyond the familiar legend. From controversial queens and eccentric kings to forgotten rulers, disastrous marriages, bizarre customs, political betrayals, and lives almost erased from the record, History Was Stranger explores what really happened, what later generations exaggerated, and what the surviving evidence can still tell us.
Because history was never as neat, dignified, or predictable as it looks in a textbook.

We talk about different species, individual animals, conservation efforts, nutrition...all kinds of stuff. This is a podcast suitable for all ages, but we will discuss topics like mating behaviors and euthanasia. If you're a fan of zoos, or have ever wondered what exactly a zookeeper does, how aquariums manage to keep all that water so clean, or just want to hear a bunch of amazing stories about incredible animals, and the people that take care of them, this is the podcast for you! Check us out online at www.rossifari.com and on all social media platforms @rossifari. Support the show at patreon.com/rossifari. Check out the merch at rossifari.redbubble.com.

title: Orchard OCD Research Podcast

description: What do we actually know about OCD and what are we still getting wrong? Orchard OCD sits down with the clinicians, academics, and researchers working at the front line of obsessive-compulsive disorder: the people running the trials, developing the treatments, and seeing patients every week. Each episode digs into what the latest research really says, where the field is heading, and what it means for people living with OCD and those who treat them. Honest conversations about a condition that's widely misunderstood, from the people who understand it best.

title: Vulnerable Podcast
author: PodCo
description:
Vulnerable with Christy Carlson Romano is a candid look at what happens after the credits roll.

Long before conversations about child stardom, burnout, reinvention, mental health, and growing up in public became commonplace, Christy was sitting down with actors, creators, former child stars, and cultural icons to talk about the parts of their stories people rarely get to hear.

Now, we’re reopening the Vulnerable archive.

In these conversations, Christy goes beyond nostalgia to explore ambition, identity, relationships, failure, resilience, and what it actually takes to build a life after the version of yourself the world thinks it knows.

Best known for Even Stevens, Kim Possible, and her years growing up on screen, Christy is now telling her own story more fully than ever. Her memoir, Once Upon a Trainwreck: The Fall and Rise of a Child Star, arrives October 6, and she returns to the screen this holiday season in Holiday Ever After.

Some of these episodes were recorded years ago. Listening to them now, with everything that has happened since, hits differently.

Welcome back to Vulnerable.

For advertising opportunities please email: brooney@podco.us

New Episodes: Monday • Wednesday • Friday
Join Karl Perkins (K.A. Perkins) as he documents the real-time journey of building the Avodah Dynamics ecosystem. The Daily Architect delivers practical insights on leadership, biblical entrepreneurship, branding, AI, financial legacy, and strategic execution. Learn from the wins, setbacks, and decisions behind building a purpose-driven business—and apply the blueprint to build your own legacy.

title: The Imad But Also Podcast
author: Imad Abdulkadir
description: The no filter, no theme, anything goes podcast where you'll hear me, Imad Abdulkadir, interviewing folks or just ranting about whatever under the sun. This could be about politics, mental health, music, social commentary you name it. If I like you and you have some story of substance to share, I'll put you on this podcast or post my own ruminations here.

title: Red Flags & Regular Coffee
author: Deliciousonde
description: Navigating your twenties and thirties is basically a full-time job where the pay is anxiety and the retirement plan is a nap. Red Flags & Regular Coffee is your weekly support group for people who keep ignoring obvious warning signs just because someone is funny or texts back in all lowercase.Join us as we roast our own catastrophically bad dating histories, questionable career moves, and the general dumpster fire of modern adulthood. It is like therapy, but cheaper, funnier, and paired with a legal dose of caffeine because raw-dogging reality without coffee is a federal offense. Warning: May contain strong language, severe denial, and sudden realizations that your type is toxic. Grab a mug and listen in before you text your ex again.

title: Dark Mafia Romance Audiobook

description:
Step into the dark, dangerous world of Dark Mafia Romance — a gripping audiobook packed with forbidden love, power, and betrayal. 🖤
This mafia romance audiobook follows a story of obsession, danger, and passion between a ruthless mob boss and the woman who dares to challenge him. Perfect for fans of dark romance, mafia romance books, enemies to lovers, and possessive alpha male stories.

If you love romance audiobooks, dark romance novels, or mafia love stories, this is a must-listen.
#DarkMafiaRomance #MafiaRomance #DarkRomance #RomanceAudiobook #EnemiesToLovers

title: Those Who Build: Leaders Reshaping Energy
author: Hydrogen Council
description:
At a time when attention often focuses on projects, policies, and market signals, Those Who Build turns the spotlight on the people making the decisions behind them.
Hosted by Hydrogen Council CEO Ivana Jemelkova, this podcast series features conversations with leaders across the global hydrogen value chain. Each episode goes beyond introductory discussions to explore what it takes to build new industries, scale emerging technologies, navigate uncertainty and create the conditions for long-term commercial success.

title: Called to Purpose
author: Mary Grace Yniguez
description:
Welcome to Called to Purpose—the podcast for faith-centered women entrepreneurs who know God has placed a calling on their life and refuse to ignore it any longer.


You know that small, still voice nudging you toward something bigger? The one that won't let you settle, stay comfortable, or keep playing small? That's not coincidence. That's God calling you to step into the purpose He created you for.


This is your space to get clear, get anchored, and align your business, brand, and life with what God has called you to do.


Each week, I'll sit down with incredible women leaders, entrepreneurs, and changemakers who have answered the call. They'll share how they first recognized God's direction, the fears they had to overcome, the lessons they learned along the way, and what happened when they finally said "yes" to their purpose.


I'm your host, Mary Grace Yniguez—a multi-passionate entrepreneur, visibility strategist, and woman who answered her calling kicking and screaming through fear, doubt, and uncertainty.


For years, I built businesses, led communities, and helped others grow. But deep down, I knew God was calling me to something greater—to help women stop building brands around trends and start building them around their calling.


Today, I help women anchor their brands in their calling so they can show up with confidence, lead with purpose, and create impact in the way God intended.


So if you've been feeling the pull, hearing the whisper, or sensing that God is calling you into a bigger assignment, you're in the right place.


Because the world doesn't need another copy of someone else. It needs the woman God created you to be.


Welcome to Called to Purpose.

Let's answer the call together.

title: The Self Project with Gaëlle
author: Gaëlle Hevey
description:
The Self Project Podcast is a space for exploring what it means to become the best version of yourself, acknowledging that self-improvement is an ongoing journey.
We delve into conversations about philosophy, self-growth, business, mindset, spirituality, and life, uncovering the questions, ideas, and experiences that deepen our understanding of ourselves and foster intentional living.
As I believe life is a continuous self-project, this podcast serves as a platform for further exploration and growth.

title: Sisters in Spirit Podcast
author: Sisters in Spirit
description: Welcome to Sisters in Spirit, a faith-filled podcast where two friends share honest conversations about Jesus, life, motherhood, purpose, and our walk with God. We don’t have all the answers, and we don’t pretend to. We’re simply two women learning, discerning, asking questions, and growing in faith one step at a time. Come meet us where we’re at and walk this journey with us. Whether you’re new to faith, curious about Christianity, returning to God, or seeking encouragement, you’ll find a safe space with no judgment, just real conversations and a desire to know Jesus more.

title: The Attracting Lasting Love Podcast
author: Roy Biancalana
description:
The Attracting Lasting Love Podcast is hosted by Roy Biancalana, a certified relationship coach, three-time #1 best-selling author and nationally-recognized expert in the field of attraction and conscious relationships. His podcast is devoted to supporting single people in their desire to attract a healthy, sustainable, intimate relationship. The perspective shared is a mindful or conscious perspective on life, love and the pursuit of intimacy.
Roy does not focus much on telling single people where to go, how to approach or what to say to a potential partner. Rather, he focuses on helping people identify and let go of the barriers, blockages and self-sabotaging patterns that keep them single. Roy's work and this podcast are in alignment with the advice given from the famous 13th century mystic poet, Rumi, who said, "Your task is not to seek love, but instead to seek and find all the barriers within yourself that you have built against it."

title: Daisy & Mabel – English Story Time for Kids

description: Warm, gentle English stories for children aged 6–10, inspired by Daisy & Mabel’s real-life adventures. Each episode supports ESL learning through simple vocabulary, clear narration, and calm storytelling. Perfect for families who want relaxed English listening practice, bedtime stories, or cosy learning moments at home.

title: Raised on Records
author: Jimmy
description: More than a melody, the music of the 1980s carries memories, stories, and cultural moments that shaped those songs. I grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area in a family that owned a record shop where the '80s unfolded one record at a time. Each episode revisits a song, its artist, the world around it, and my memories of the decade. And whether you lived through the '80s or discovered its music years later, its familiar songs may still have something new to reveal. Because a record can do more than remind us of where we've been. Sometimes, it can rewind us to a time we thought we'd forgotten.

title: Lola & Lani
author: Merlola Bordeaux, Alanis Percocet
description: Merlola Bordeaux and Alanis Percocet live in a strange and wonderful town called Cityville, a place made for and made by drag queens! description:
Balls, Bails, Banter with Stu and Jim is a light-hearted, laugh-out-loud podcast celebrating the glorious chaos of village cricket at Dedham Cricket Club.
Join lifelong club stalwarts Jim and Stu as they dive into the week’s matches, questionable umpiring decisions, heroic (and not-so-heroic) performances, and the timeless traditions that make grassroots cricket what it is. From collapsing batting orders and miraculous last-wicket stands to teas that outshine the cricket itself, nothing is off limits.

title: Pull Over… We Need To Talk
author: Lauren and Abbie
description:
Pull Over… We Need To Talk is the podcast that started with a TikTok idea… and somehow ended with microphones in a parked car.
Join sisters-in-law Lauren and Abbie for honest, funny conversations about life, relationships, hyperfixations, questionable purchases and everything in between. It’s like eavesdropping on two friends oversharing.
So… pull over. We need to talk.

title: Life On Your Terms- Quick Hits with Autumn
author: Autumn Schmidt
description:
Life On Your Terms: Quick Hits with Autumn offers 5 minute episodes for successful women who are tired of second-guessing themselves, overthinking every decision, worrying about what everyone else thinks, and knowing what they want—only to talk themselves out of it.
In short, straight-to-the-point episodes, Autumn Schmidt breaks down the patterns that keep capable women stuck and helps you understand yourself differently, trust what you already know, and actually move on the life you want.
We'll talk self-trust, people-pleasing, intuition, boundaries, confidence, identity, your next chapter, and what happens when the life you built no longer fits the woman you've become.
It's not about becoming someone else-
It's about trusting and working with yourself again. 
Know what you want. Trust yourself. F*ck what they think. Go get it. Stay Difficult.
Life on your terms starts here.

title: The TazTalks Show

description:
The TazTalks Show is a platform for Sheffield and the people shaping the city.
Conversations with creatives, founders and local voices — we get into what they’re building, creating and doing.
There’s a lot happening here that deserves more attention. Our goal is simple: put Sheffield on the map, one story at a time.
New episodes regularly. Find TazTalks on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

title: Are You Rubbish
author: dave rampage
description: Are You Rubbish? is a hilarious comedy podcast that playfully tests just how "trashy" or absurd your everyday habits really are. Through casual banter, wildly irrelevant yet deeply relatable questions, and unfiltered humor, the hosts unpack silly life moments, questionable choices, and little secrets that leave you wondering: "Is it just me, or am I actually rubbish?"

title: Light It Up With Dr Lara Goode
author: Lara
description:
Light It Up with Dr Lara Goode is where women stop shrinking, start questioning the rules and finally say the things we’ve been conditioned to keep quiet.

Hosted by osteopath, business owner and late-diagnosed ADHD fire cracker Dr Lara Goode. This podcast is packed with honest, unfiltered conversations about ambition, identity, motherhood, relationships, burnout, reinvention and what happens when you decide the “good girl” script no longer fits.

Each episode features bold women who have gone against the grain, challenged expectations and built lives that feel true to them, even when it meant disappointing people, changing direction or burning the rulebook entirely.

Expect real stories, uncomfortable truths, plenty of humour and the occasional overshare.

Because sometimes you just need to light it up.

description:
Most of us spend a lifetime avoiding the conversations that can lead to real change—but what if facing our inner dialogue could become one of our most powerful tools for growth?


Welcome to Conversations Create Change, a therapist-led podcast hosted by therapist and mental-health content creator Cynthia Agyeman-Anane. Through honest, meaningful conversations, Cynthia and her guests explore the experiences that shape us, helping us better understand ourselves and our relationships while healing and moving toward lasting change.


Season 1 brings together Black therapists, mental-health professionals, creatives, and community voices for grounded discussions about grief, identity, relationships, motherhood, anxiety, chronic illness, self-discovery and healing. Together, these conversations create a space for real talk, reflection, growth and healing—within ourselves, our relationships, and our communities.

title: We Explain by YouSustain

Sustainability can feel a bit... overwhelming. New acronyms every week, headlines that never tell the full story, everyone's got an opinion.

for the life ahead. That is possible that your latter years can be greater.

title: he Day Hunters: Chronicles of the Sky Runners by Adam Schmid
author: Momentum Media Advertising
description: Prepare for a thrilling, two-thousand-year journey through ancient conflict and modern-day espionage as Vatican agent Gabriel and his partner Rebecca race to stop a vengeful werewolf pack mobilized by a devastating historical lie. I am your host, Paul Indrigo. Realtor, Podcaster and Film/Tv Location Scout. Since my early days in real estate, I would include famous film locations on my local tours. Ontario’s dramatic skylines, historic small towns, rustic cottage country, and industrial architecture make it one of the most sought-after filming destinations on the planet. Join me as we step onto active sets, trace movie magic back to its real-world origins, and breakdown how local landmarks are transformed for the screen. From the bustling streets of Toronto double-timing as Manhattan to historic heritage sites stepping in for fantasy realms, we explore the stories, the local secrets, and the exact coordinates where cinematic history was made.

Every episode dives deep into iconic film sets, featuring interviews with location managers, local historians, cast and crew members, and fans who go location-hunting in their own backyards. Put on your headphones, pull up your map, and let's go behind the scenes of Hollywood North!

Featured Titles Covered on the Show. Blockbuster & Oscar-Winning Movies:


  • The Shape of Water – See how Hamilton and Toronto (including the Elgin Theatre) set the atmospheric tone for Guillermo del Toro’s Oscar-winning romance.
  • IT & IT Chapter Two – Discover how the picturesque town of Port Hope was transformed into the eerie town of Derry, Maine.
  • Good Will Hunting – Take a trip to the University of Toronto, which doubled for Harvard and MIT.
  • Mean Girls – Tour the Toronto schools and homes behind the ultimate 2000s teen comedy.
  • Scott Pilgrim vs. The World – Trace Scott's steps through Casa Loma, Lee's Palace, and the Wychwood neighborhood.
  • Shazam! & Suicide Squad – Explore how downtown Toronto doubled for fictional comic book metropolises.
Binge-Worthy TV Series:
  • The Handmaid's Tale – Walk through the real Ontario locations—from Cambridge to Toronto's City Hall—used to build the haunting world of Gilead.
  • Memory of a Killer – Follow the journey of a hit man facing alzheimers as the show films in areas across Ontario including the Danforth and Port Hope.
  • The Boys – Spot the GTA landmarks, arenas, and heritage sites used for Vought Headquarters and epic superhero showdowns.
  • Suits – Uncover how Toronto’s Financial District seamlessly passed for New York City for nine seasons.
  • Reacher – Trace Jack Reacher's path across Kingston, Pickering, and rural Southwestern Ontario.
  • The Umbrella Academy – Explore the historic homes, grand halls, and gritty alleyways across Hamilton and Toronto.
  • Schitt's Creek – Take a road trip to Goodwood, Ontario, the real-life backdrop for Rosebud Motel and the town's beloved main street.
  • Star Trek: Discovery – See how Ontario soundstages and unique brutalist architecture bring distant galaxies to life.
Subscribe now on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, or wherever you listen to podcasts, and never view your favorite screen moments the same way again!

title: Great Detectives and Their Methods
author: Dream audio books
description:
Great Detectives and Their Methods by George Dilnot invites listeners into the practical world of criminal investigation before modern databases, digital surveillance, and advanced forensic laboratories. Rather than celebrating fictional sleuths, Dilnot examines real detectives and the working habits that allowed them to solve difficult and sometimes baffling cases.
Across accounts involving robbery, fraud, confidence schemes, disappearance, and murder, the book explores how skilled investigators learned to observe people, places, and evidence. Some detectives depended on patience and an exceptional memory for detail. Others relied on careful questioning, informants, disguise, surveillance, written records, or a strong understanding of human behavior. Their approaches were different, but their success usually came from discipline, persistence, and the willingness to test every assumption.
The audiobook also reveals how demanding detective work could be during a period when information moved slowly and communication tools were limited. Investigators often had to follow suspects across cities, compare small pieces of evidence, identify contradictions in apparently convincing stories, and continue working when no obvious solution was available. A forgotten object, an unusual habit, or a minor inconsistency could become the clue that changed an entire investigation.
Although some procedures reflect the attitudes and limitations of the early twentieth century, the book’s central principles remain compelling. Effective detection requires clear reasoning, attention to detail, knowledge of human motives, and respect for evidence rather than speculation.
Great Detectives and Their Methods is recommended for listeners interested in historical true crime, criminology, police history, criminal psychology, and real-life mysteries. Informative and accessible, this complete audiobook presents detection not as magic, but as a craft developed through experience, intelligence, courage, and relentless curiosity.
Listeners will discover why successful investigators rarely depended on a single brilliant deduction; instead, they combined methodical preparation, local knowledge, teamwork, and steady attention over time to uncover truth.

Sport, relationships, parenting, work, creativity — different arenas, same question: how do you understand your drama, manage it and get more joy out of life?
Real stories. Real tools. Clean Language. #DramaFree.

title: Winning With Better Food

Winning with Better Food is a business podcast from Eat Well Global for leading food producers, retailers, and operators focused on turning health and nutrition into real growth.
Each episode unpacks a commercial case study with the operators behind the strategy to discover what drove velocity or store visits, what consumers responded to, what built trust, and where the economics made or broke the plan.

title: The Better Man Project Podcast
author: Christopher Akinsanya
description:
🔥 The Better Man Project
What does it really mean to be a man?
The Better Man Project is a place for honest conversations about manhood, mental health, relationships, faith, purpose, healing, and growth. We talk about struggles men often keep to themselves, the pressure to always be strong, and what it takes to become better. No masks. No pretending we have all the answers. Real stories, real struggles, and real conversations. 
Whether you’re a man finding your way or someone who loves one, there’s a seat here for you. Pull up a chair. Welcome to the Fire. 🔥 The Journey to better starts today.

title: What's Your Ex?
author: Marilie Daniels
description:
What's Your EX? with Marilie — The Pivot Isn't Starting Over

You have an ex you've never talked about.

It's not a person. It's the career that let you go. The dream you buried. The version of yourself you walked away from — and still think about at 2 a.m.

Here's what nobody tells you: none of it was wasted.

What's Your EX? is the podcast about the pivot — career change, reinvention, and second chances — the show about who we used to be, and how it was all preparation for who we are becoming.

Because here's the whole idea: the pivot isn't about starting over. It's about finally seeing what you were being prepared for.

We all carry exes that have nothing to do with romance. Ex-careers. Ex-dreams. Ex-titles. Ex-versions of ourselves we've outgrown or been forced to leave behind. And most of us quietly file those chapters under "failure," "wasted time," or "the detour." This show exists to change that. To take the parts of your story you're a little embarrassed about — and reveal them for what they actually were: preparation.

Every week, Marilie sits down for one honest, warm, no-fluff conversation that flips how you see a chapter of your life. Some weeks it's about feeling behind. Some weeks it's about fear, or reinvention, or who you are when a title disappears, or finding the nerve to begin again. Different angle every time — same through line: you were never starting from scratch. You were starting from experience.

This isn't another motivational podcast telling you to erase your past and hustle harder. It's a space to breathe, re-frame, and reclaim what you'd written off — and walk away with one simple, practical idea you can actually use that week.

If you've ever felt stuck, felt behind, changed direction, or wondered who you are without your job title — this is your show. It's for the career changers and the late bloomers. The ones starting over at 30, at 40, at 55. Anyone in a season of transition, reinvention, burnout recovery, or quiet personal growth who needs to hear that their story was building toward something all along.

Because sometimes the bravest, most freeing thing you'll ever do is look back at everything you've lived — and realize not one bit of it was wasted.

So — What's Your Ex?

Hit follow, and let's go find out. Together.

New episodes weekly. Share this podcast with someone who needs it.
#WhatsYourEX · @iammariliedaniels

title: Laid Bare
author: Gill Baird
description:
Laid Bare is a candid, behind‑the‑scenes podcast that pulls back the curtain on the world of cosmetic surgery. Each episode dives into the realities patients rarely see - from how surgical teams make decisions, to the safety standards, ethics, and regulations that shape every procedure.

Through open conversations with medical directors, surgeons, anaesthetists, nurses, and patient‑care experts, the podcast explores what really happens before, during, and after surgery. Listeners gain insight into patient selection, BMI considerations, surgical planning, complication management, and the honest reasons why not everyone is approved for treatment.

Beyond the operating theatre, Laid Bare tackles the evolving landscape of private healthcare, the impact of social media, the boundaries of filming live surgeries, and the expectations patients bring to their cosmetic journeys. It also highlights emerging services - from aesthetics and laser treatments to dentistry and minor procedures - offering a transparent look at how modern clinics operate.

Unfiltered, informative, and grounded in real clinical experience, Laid Bare is designed to educate, empower, and give listeners a truthful understanding of what safe, ethical cosmetic surgery looks like today.

title: Wise Scientists
author: David Lorimer
description:
Philosopher-physicist Ravi Ravindra notes that according to all the sages, there are many levels of reality subtler than the mind. So, any enterprise wholly driven by the mind—including science, philosophy, and theology—cannot connect with these subtler levels of reality. In order to relate with these subtle levels one needs to rely on direct perception, not on thought.
Hence, the need to open up and enhance the quality of perception and being among scientists. Then they are more likely to attain knowledge which is closer to wisdom. A wise scientist is interested in truth - which is a subtle combination of knowledge and compassion.
In this Wise Scientists podcast series, Ravi engages in dialogue with leading scientists about the need for more wisdom in society in general, and specifically among scientists due to its cultural power and influence as well as the speed of current technological developments, for instance in AI.
Links
Scientific and Medical Network – https://scientificandmedical.net
Galileo Commission – https://galileocommission.org
Ravi Ravindra - https://ravindra.ca/

Some episodes go deep into the science. Others feature conversations with experts, entrepreneurs, clinicians, athletes, and people with stories worth hearing. But every episode comes back to the same question:
**How do we become better physically, mentally, and spiritually—and make the years ahead some of our best?**
This isn't about chasing perfection.
It's about pursuing your prime.
**Prime Pursuit — Better Health. Deeper Purpose.**

description:
The forgotten (body) part of sustainability transitions. On why systems can't be at peace with the living world if the people running them are at war inside. I help write the rules for sustainable finance. Then I go dancing. This is a podcast about why I think those are the same job.

Each episode is a conversation with someone working somewhere in that gap: neuroscience and embodiment, ecopsychology and deep ecology, doughnut economics and degrowth, ritual and grief, indigenous wisdom and future literacy, inner development goals and systems change, system-oriented design and regenerative leadership.

For people who believe we as a species have the potential to do better: Live at peace with ourselves, with each other, and with the biosphere we have never once been separate from. For people who long for, dream of and would like to co-create Our Common Future. 

Your host: Kaja Koppang — systemic designer, leads the sustainability work for an alliance of Norwegian banks, co-led the first Nordic sustainability reporting standard, and a Movement Medicine teacher in training. title: Connecting Wealth with Purpose
author: connectingwealthwpurpose
description: Do you want to use your wealth as a tool to enrich your life and the lives of those around you? From legacy and family priorities to empowering the causes you care about; our conversations can inspire you. You work hard. You earn good money. And yet something still feels uncertain about depending on that one paycheck forever.
Welcome to the Money Makin Mamas Show — the podcast for professional women who are ready to transition from paycheck dependency into single family real estate investing without quitting their jobs.

One property can change everything. Let us show you how.

Each episode breaks down the business behind the music, including artist development, label economics, distribution, licensing, publishing rights, master recordings, royalty structures, streaming platforms, touring, branding, promotion, audience growth, catalog acquisitions, negotiations, contracts, and the changing relationship between artists and the companies that support them.

The podcast also examines the executives, entrepreneurs, producers, managers, investors, technology companies, and major industry players influencing where the music business goes next. Episodes may explore historic deals, modern streaming economics, independent artists, major labels, music technology, intellectual property, marketing strategies, mergers, acquisitions, and the decisions that can turn songs and catalogs into valuable long-term assets.

Whether you are an artist, songwriter, producer, manager, label owner, music entrepreneur, investor, or simply fascinated by the business behind the industry, The Music Business Podcast delivers accessible insight into record labels, streaming, publishing, royalties, marketing, deals, and music industry strategy.

Welcome to The RAID Party, the cybersecurity podcast where every guest joins as a different class, bringing unique skills to defend the digital realm. From red and blue teamers to threat hunters, incident responders, malware analysts, security architects, and CISOs, each episode shows how every role contributes to the mission.
No single class wins alone. Victory comes from strategy, teamwork, and stories from those who've faced the toughest encounters.
Hosted by Josh Shepard, Director of RAID at RADICL.
Gather your party.

title: Adulting101 Masterclass:  Career, Money and Life Skills School Failed To Teach
author: Heather Redisch
description:
Adulting101 Masterclass is the life skills podcast for young adults navigating the real world — and for the parents who want to see them succeed in life and managers who want to help them thrive in business.
Because the real world doesn’t come with a manual.
But this show does.
Hosted by Heather Redisch, talent development expert and founder of Adulting101 Masterclass, This podcast delivers practical, no-nonsense tools for the life skills school failed  to teach—but the real world expects you to know.
From navigating the job search and building your career to managing money, understanding the unwritten rules of the workplace, building self confidence, communicating clearly, and handling the everyday logistics of real life, Adulting101 is a no-judgement resource to learn the basics from your peers, experts and mentors.
Whether you are a recent graduate, a parent trying to support your young adult, or a leader managing younger generations for the first time, Adulting101 helps bridge the gap between what school taught and what real life demands.
Each episode delivers real, actionable strategies you can use right away.
No theory.
No fluff.
Just the stuff that actually matters when you’re figuring out how to become a functioning adult.
Adulting101 covers:
Communication and confidence—setting boundaries, speaking up for yourself, and navigating hard conversations
Career and workplace skills—professionalism, networking, asking for a raise, reading the room
Financial basics—budgeting, credit, taxes, student loans, and saving for real life
Life logistics—insurance, renting an apartment, healthcare, and all the things nobody taught you
What parents can do (and stop doing) to raise capable, confident adults
What managers need to understand about the newest generation entering the workforce
You belong here!

title: The Wellness Digest
author: Hannah & Lena Kleinfeld
description:
The Wellness Digest is a weekly reset for anyone trying to feel well without turning wellness into a full-time job.

Hosted by sisters Hannah and Lena Kleinfeld, the founders behind Omni-Biotic U.S., the show draws on their unique perspective working alongside microbiome scientists, clinicians, and thousands of people navigating symptoms that are often misunderstood, dismissed, or left unexplained.

Each week, they explore the patterns shaping modern health, from burnout and nervous system overload to hormone shifts, skin changes, fatigue, and digestion, and what these signals may be trying to tell us.

Through expert conversations and honest discussions, Hannah and Lena share what they are learning through their work, their own health journeys, and the practitioners they trust, offering a clearer, more grounded understanding of how to support your body in real life.

The gut remains a throughline, but the mission is bigger. To help you cut through noise, return to foundations, and better understand what it takes to feel well today.

Through raw storytelling, social commentary, and the voices of those left behind, Hunt The Hunter explores police violence, accountability, family trauma, and the lengths people will go to when the institutions meant to protect them fail.
This is not simply a story about one death. It is a story about what happens to a family when justice becomes something they have to chase themselves.

What does it mean to bear the spark of the Creator in a fractured world?

title: Why we miss people who hurt us

description:
Why Do We Miss People Who Hurt Us?

Have you ever wondered why you still miss someone who hurt you? Why does your mind remember the good moments even when you know the relationship caused you pain?

Sometimes, we don’t miss the person who hurt us. We miss the version of them we loved, the memories we shared, the comfort they once gave us, or the person we hoped they would become. Our minds naturally hold on to emotional connections, even when those connections are no longer healthy.

In this episode, we explore the psychology behind missing people who hurt us, why our brains struggle to let go, why we remember the good times more than the painful ones, and why letting go doesn’t always mean you stopped caring.

Because sometimes, missing someone is not a sign that you should go back. It is simply a sign that something once mattered to you.

title: Talking With Umaa

description: Talking With Umaa is a curious corner for the things we leave unnamed. Host Umaa Thampu is a Gestalt psychotherapist working at the intersection of therapy, identity, culture and power. Each episode is one unhurried, rigorous conversation with a practitioner, writer, scholar or artist whose thinking changes how we understand the inner life — and what history, race, class, migration, queerness and power are doing inside it. This is not a therapy-advice show. There are no tips and no quick fixes. It is a thinking space: guests bring the concepts they have built, Umaa puts those concepts under pressure, 'Where does this idea fail?' and 'Who does it leave out?' Every episode ends with something you can take into your own practice, workplace or family before the next one arrives. Who it's for: therapists, counsellors, psychologists, supervisors and trainees who want language for what their training never covered. Educators, organisers, HR professionals and faith leaders who need more than a slogan. And anyone who reads seriously about power and belonging and wants a conversation that does not flatten it. What you'll hear: racial dynamics and racial trauma. Migration, caste, class, queerness, faith and belonging. What happens in the body when race or power enters the room? Complicity, harm and repair. The limits of clinical models that pretend context does not exist. And the specific, human, unexpected stories underneath all of it. How it works: we start with where a guest comes from and how they see. We put that lens inside the real systems they work in — where those systems hold people and where they fail them. Then we test the ideas rather than admire them and turn them into questions you can use. Released in seasons. New episodes and the notes, resources and reflection prompts that go with them are announced first through the Talking With Umaa newsletter. Umaa Thampu is MBACP accredited, trained at the Gestalt Centre London, and a member of the Black, African and Asian Therapy Network.

title: Liftoff Journeys
author: Jeanniey Walden
description:
Liftoff Journeys isn’t about polished success stories. It’s about the moments before success makes sense.

It was inspired by my three-year-old who told me, “I want to be a bubble bather when I grow up."   I realized that what she saw was that a bubble bath created joy, helped people, and made others feel good.Her instinct to do this in every roles she has had never disappeared.

This moment revealed something powerful to me: it’s the moments before success that shape who we become.Hosted by Jeanniey Walden, Liftoff Journeys features honest conversations with leaders, founders, and executives about how they actually built their lives and careers, through real decisions, detours, doubts, and defining moments.No bios. No highlight reels. Just authentic choices, inspired action, and relatable human experience.

At its core, the show reflects the mission of Liftoff Enterprises: helping leaders grow with confidence, clarity, and trust - in themselves and with others. These conversations echo the ideas behind my book The Trust Threshold: the point where self-doubt turns into momentum and leadership shifts from performance to presence.

There’s no single path to growth, but there are patterns.If you’ve ever wondered what happens before it all clicks, this podcast is for you.This is Liftoff Journeys.

title: New Teacher, Big Impact
author: Daryl Williams Jr
description:
Introducing the "New Teacher, Big Impact" podcast, where we equip new teachers with the tools to become more effective while prioritizing their well-being.

Have you ever felt burnt out, unsupported, or like you had to change who you are to make an impact in the classroom? Daryl knows exactly how that feels, and wants you to know that you don't have to struggle with those feelings. Join Daryl and other special guest educators as we explore the transformative power of discovering your "Teacher ID" – a journey that took him from being a terrible teacher to becoming a two-time Teacher of the Year.

In each episode, we'll dive deep into the core principles of teaching excellence:

Identify Your Dream: Reignite your passion for teaching by casting a vision that aligns with your purpose.

Illuminate Your Differences: Embrace your uniqueness and learn how to leverage it to make a profound impact on your students.

Ignore Your Doubters: Overcome self-limiting beliefs and fortify your mindset against external hurdles.

Improve Your Data: Master the Six Pillars of Effective Instruction:
1. Encourage: Create a classroom culture that supports student growth.

2. Engage: Manage the classroom, and craft lessons that capture attention.

3. Empower: Deliver content in a way that leads to information retention.

4. Evaluate: Utilize data to make informed decisions about instruction.

5. Extend: Continue growing in your learning and professional development.

6. Endure: Prioritize your well-being so that you can keep showing up.

Join us on the "New Teacher, Big Impact" podcast and learn how to be the teacher you've always wanted to be while making a lasting impact on your students' lives.
